text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the treatment reference, the case reference, the case attributes the scope test needs (owner, queue and team), the field IDs the screen will show and, where the decision is the authority of an approval, the approval level written on the treatment with the decision code, the regulation item, the product group, the principal, the loss percentage and the loss amount; it answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the matrix version, the masking answer per field ID, the scope result, the access-entry reference and, for an approval, the level, the delegation row, the limit version and the outcome. The Treatment and offer and Case record letters are read from the policy pack at the matrix version in force, loaded as rows, and never tabulated in code.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and the TSD appendix does not, and the TSD RBAC matrix tabulates only three capability areas, so the request, the answer and the two capability areas have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them empty would stop the story.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 T3.2, T6.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 A2.4, A2.7 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-004 sections 10 and 12
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 7; section 10 Authority; section 11 Data; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead at the contract review of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, with the matrix owner for the two capability areas
impact: A different shape changes the controller, the contract fake and every caller's client only; the decision codes, the refusal messages and the entry content do not change.

text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits takes decisionCode, regulationItem, productGroup, principal, lossPct, lossAmount and onDate as query parameters under the base /api/recovery/access/v1, and answers level, delegationLimitId, limitVersion, holderUserId, substituteUserId and outcome, where outcome is one of COVERED, NOT_COVERED, NO_HOLDER, NO_AMOUNT_LIMIT and RELATED_PARTY.
why: Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operation and no Appendix T-A entry carries it, so the field set has to be fixed as a default; the fields are the columns of delegation_limit that the lookup needs and the answers the FSD A2.6 ACs describe.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 T3.1 and T-A.1; FSD P4 A2.6 AC-ALT-P4-006-01, AC-ALT-P4-006-02 and AC-EXC-P4-006-04
applied_in: Section 4 Flow steps 8 to 10; section 7 AC4 and AC5; section 12.1; section 12.8; section 13 Build steps 6 and 7
confirm: Solution architect when API-P4-022 is added to the P4 API specification; RWB-P4-E2013-APP must answer the same request
impact: A renamed field changes the controller, the repository query and the rwb-decision client only; the outcome values are shared with RWB-P4-E2013-APP and must be fixed once for both.

text: The delegation lookup answers against the limit version whose valid_from is not after the approval date and whose valid_to is empty or not before it, and names that version in the answer; DOA-2026.11 is the version loaded in SIT from 30 November 2026, and no code holds a version label.
why: The version in force is a property of the loaded rows and the environments are loaded at different times, so a hard-coded label would answer a level against a version that may not be in force on the date asked.
read: FSD P4 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01 and AC-ALT-P4-006-02; TSD P4 T3.1; Temporal and Drools Design slide 6 notes
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 9; section 9 State transitions; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Business lead and the DoA load owner at the RWB-P4-E1038-APP acceptance
impact: If an environment is loaded with a different version the answer names that version and no code changes; a wrong load is a data defect of the DoA story, not a build change here.

text: The gateway-bff composite route of SCR-14 asks rwb-case for the case, rwb-treatment for the treatment and rwb-access for the decision, and the SCR-03 timer panel route asks rwb-case for the timer list and rwb-access for the decision, each one hop; this story serves only the decision and accepts the field IDs in the request, so the route names whatever the screen shows.
why: No document lists the fields of the two screens, and the decision must not fix a field list in code that the route cannot change without a build.
read: Architecture v5 slides 10, 14 and 41; FSD P4 Screens; Legacy RWB-E2-004 section 15
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1; section 15 Screens and states
confirm: Solution architect and the gateway-bff owner when the two composite routes are published
impact: A wider field list needs no build here, only a route change, unless a field added later is a personal field; that would add a masking row and change the masking answer.

text: The database login of rwb-access is referred to as the rwb-access login (DP-02) until the platform DB story fixes its name, its grants and the owner of its schema objects.
why: DP-02 requires one login per service and no document names it, so the story needs a stable way to refer to it without inventing a name that another document would then contradict.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41 notes; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; TSD P4 T1
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 13 Database and migrations
confirm: ACE team at the platform DB story of DP-02
impact: A name fixed later changes the migration and the connection configuration only; no decision, message or entry content changes.
